meta.scope: Water and electricity costs for both properties. The owner asked for projections of these costs out to the inheritance window. Every published rate below is read from the utility's own tariff; every usage quantity is an assumption and is labelled as such.

water.label: Retail water providers in Cupertino
water.value: Three separate systems: California Water Service (northeastern portion), San Jose Water Company (southeastern portion), and the City of Cupertino municipal system (western portion), the last of which is operated by San Jose Water Company under a lease extended to 2036
water.note: Material finding: the rate that applies to Property C depends on which of the three service areas it sits in. That cannot be determined from a ZIP code alone — it requires the City's Water Service Provider GIS map. Confirm before budgeting.

water.note: SFPUC confirms a stormwater component exists and that residential customers are charged on a simplified three-tier structure based on net parcel size. The tier dollar amounts were not located in the retrieved pages. Required to complete the bill; left blank.

water.label: Owner-reported monthly water cost, all three units
water.note: Cross-check on the Utilities page: using the verified SFPUC rates above, this range corresponds to roughly 9 CCF per month of total water use across three units on a 1-inch meter, before the stormwater component. That is a plausible figure, so the owner's number is corroborated rather than contradicted by the tariff.

electricity.label: Which solar billing rule applies to the existing system
electricity.note: This is the highest-value open question on the electricity side and it turns entirely on the interconnection date. Systems with a completed interconnection application submitted before 2023-04-15 are on NEM 2.0 and keep near-retail export credits for 20 years from interconnection. Systems applied for on or after that date are on the Net Billing Tariff, where exports earn hourly avoided-cost values. The citation for the 2023-04-15 boundary was found only in secondary sources in this pass, so it is not asserted here. Confirm the interconnection date from the PG&E interconnection agreement or the original installer paperwork.

electricity.label: Owner-reported net electricity cost
electricity.value: Net credit of roughly 10 to 20 USD per month
electricity.note: A small net credit is only consistent with NEM 2.0 (near-retail export credit) or with a large system under the Net Billing Tariff. The distinction matters enormously for the holding-cost projections and is unresolved.

electricity.label: PG&E residential rate per kilowatt-hour
electricity.note: Not retrieved from PG&E's published tariff or from the CPUC in this pass. Aggregator sites publish figures around 0.33 to 0.55 USD/kWh depending on plan and season, and reference a CPUC Public Advocates Office quarterly report and PG&E Advice Letter 7846-E, but none of that was confirmed against the primary document. Left blank.

electricity.label: PG&E fixed monthly charge on residential bills
electricity.note: Secondary sources describe an income-graduated Base Services Charge introduced in 2026 replacing an older fixed charge. Not confirmed against a PG&E tariff. Left blank. Relevant because a fixed charge cannot be offset by solar exports, which caps how negative an electricity bill can go.

electricity.label: Owner-reported monthly electricity cost, all three units
electricity.note: Owner reports this range. Not verifiable without the bill.
